findings.title: All functional and technical success criteria are covered by tasks
findings.description: Every functional requirement (PASS/FAIL output, `missing:` lines, doctype handling, multi-file ordering, all exit-2 cases including valid-before-missing and `cf guides update`, `--json` contract, worktree template resolution) and every technical requirement (normalization unit tests, real-template test asserting `## Overview` and `### Verification Walkthrough`, real-slice command test, build/lint/full test and line limits) maps to a concrete task with a stated success condition. The Verification Walkthrough steps 1–6 are covered by Task 5, including the parity sweep and "no unexplained DIFF" success gate.

findings.title: Test-with pattern and commit placement are correct
findings.description: Each implementation task is immediately followed by its dedicated test task and then a semantic commit (Task 2→2T→2C, 3→3T→3C, 4→4T→4C). Test tasks use inline strings for the pure validator and the real template/files for the file and command layers, matching the design's pure-vs-file-layer decision. Commits land at tested points rather than after every task or only at the end; Tasks 5C and 6C are correctly gated on actual file changes.

findings.title: Sequencing, scoping, and proportionality are sound
findings.description: Dependencies run strictly forward (constant → pure validator → file layer → subcommand → verification → docs) with no circular dependencies; each task is independently completable by a junior AI given the design's contracts. No task widens the frozen output/JSON/exit contract, adds the excluded `cf check` wiring or `SLICE_DESIGN_TEMPLATE` override, or does the excluded guide-side edits. One task file, 16 bounded tasks, and step detail that mirrors the design rather than inventing implementation constraints are proportionate to a 168-line-script port with three new source files and three test files.
